recipes.name: Crunchy Korean nut candy (Yeot-gangjeong: 엿강정)
ingredients: 3 cups variety of unsalted roasted nuts
⅓ cup store bought rice syrup
instructions: Put the nuts in a mesh strainer over a bowl. Shake to remove any broken or dusty bits.
Place parchment paper (12 inch x 14 inch) on a large cutting board.
Heat the rice syrup over medium high heat for about 2 minutes until it starts bubbling. Reduce the heat to medium.

Occasionally stir the syrup with a wooden spoon for 6 to 7 minutes as the bubbles get bigger and bigger, until it gets to the point where it is almost one big bubble covering the whole top of the pan like a balloon (should be about 220°F). Remove from the heat.
Add the nuts and mix it all up with a wooden spoon.
While it’s still soft and warm, quickly transfer the mixture to the center of the parchment paper on the cutting board.
Lift the edges of the paper and cover the hot candy. Press and shape the molten candy into a rough rectangle, about 6 by 7 inches. Shape and flatten it with both hands and/or a rolling pin.
Wrap it in the paper and flip it upside down. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
Cut it into small pieces, and serve.
If you have leftovers, wrap each piece of candy in a candy wrapper and put them all into a plastic bag. Freeze or keep it in a cool place.
Heat the syrup over medium heat in a small pan for about 2 minutes until it starts bubbling.
Stir with a wooden spoon for another 2 minutes until the bubbles are a little larger.
When you lift your wooden spoon in the air, some syrup should drips and form into thin threads (should be about 220°F).
Remove from the heat. Add the nuts and mix it all up with a wooden spoon.
While it’s still soft and warm, quickly transfer the mixture to the center of the parchment paper on the cutting board.
Lift the edges of the paper and cover the hot candy. Press and shape the molten candy into a rectangle about 2 by 6 inches. Shape and flatten it with both hands and/or a rolling pin.
Wrap it in the paper and flip it upside down. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
Cut it into small pieces and serve.
If you have leftovers, wrap each piece of candy in a candy wrapper and put them all into a plastic bag. Freeze or keep it in a cool place.
